headline: COBRE PANAMA TRAIN 3 BACK ONLINE — First Quantum Q2 Earnings Jump 655% to US$136M; First Copper Concentrate Shipment Due August 2026 (TSX: FM)
snippet: First Quantum Minerals (TSX: FM) reported Q2 2026 results showing net earnings surging to US$136 million from US$18 million in Q2 2025 — a 655% increase — on revenue up 8% to US$1.5 billion and EBITDA up 23% to US$400 million, as the company processed 100,487 tonnes of copper at a C1 cash cost of $2.84 per pound. The headline catalyst is Cobre Panama: the 350,000-tonne-per-year mine — shut since late 2023 following Panama's political protests that cost approximately 1% of global copper supply — successfully recommissioned its Train 3 processing line ahead of schedule in Q2, producing 3,216 tonnes of copper from stockpiled ore following Panama's April 2026 authorization, with the first concentrate shipment now targeted for August 2026 and 30,000–40,000 tonnes expected from the stockpile processing phase. For copper supply watchers tracking the $6.44/lb structural deficit thesis, Cobre Panama's phased return is the most important single mine-level development of 2026 — with Panama's decision on full restart expected after the stockpile phase, which will determine whether the mine's full 350,000-tonne-per-year contribution returns to global copper supply before 2028.

headline: 1911 GOLD BAKER DISCOVERY: 36.44 g/t Au OVER 1.1M — New Zone Added to True North Manitoba; 720m High-Grade Strike Targets Q4 2026 Resource Update (TSXV: AUMB)
snippet: 1911 Gold Corporation (TSXV: AUMB) announced on July 30 that 30 drill holes (8,656 metres) at the True North Gold Project in southeastern Manitoba returned high-grade intercepts from three near-infrastructure targets — 5.99 g/t Au over 4.90 metres at Shore, 15.89 g/t Au over 2.70 metres at SAM Southeast, and 36.44 g/t Au over 1.10 metres at the newly defined Baker zone — with gold mineralization confirmed along 720 metres of strike at depths approaching 975 metres within the SAM gabbro, all adjacent to existing underground infrastructure. The Baker discovery is the key finding: a new mineralized zone not previously included in the global resource model, which will now be incorporated into an updated resource estimate targeted for Q4 2026. At $4,086 gold, Baker's 36.44 g/t intercept represents approximately US$4,680 per tonne in-situ value and demonstrates the exploration upside remaining at an asset with established mine infrastructure — lowering the marginal cost of converting each new ounce to a mineable resource.

headline: ABITIBI METALS DISTRICT GROWS: VMS SYSTEM FOUND 1.5KM WEST OF B26 — Zinc-Silver Horizon at 400m Depth; Only 3 of 7 Regional Targets Tested So Far (TSXV: AMQFF)
snippet: Abitibi Metals Corp. (TSXV: AMQFF), a Discovery Silver-backed copper-zinc developer, announced on July 29 that drill hole 1274-26-383 — the first systematic test of the B26 property's regional potential — intersected a new volcanogenic massive sulphide (VMS) zinc-silver mineralized zone approximately 1.5 kilometres west of the B26 Deposit at 400 metres vertical depth, confirming the favourable felsic volcanic host package extends well beyond the known deposit footprint. Three of the seven high-priority regional targets identified through historical reinterpretation and the company's 2025 VTEM-MAG airborne survey were tested in this first program; downhole Pulse EM surveying will evaluate off-hole conductors before a follow-up campaign. For investors tracking Abitibi's B26 project — which has returned up to 3.63% copper and 8.16% CuEq at the central deposit — finding a VMS zinc-silver system 1.5km away in the same geological package confirms a multi-system cluster that could expand the district's total resource potential well beyond the current B26 deposit boundary.

headline: ANTIMONY DISCOVERY IN NEW BRUNSWICK, 21.3m AT 3.0 g/t Au IN QUEBEC — Globex Royalty Network Delivers Three Partner Results in One Session (TSX: GMX)
snippet: Globex Mining Enterprises Inc. (TSX: GMX) announced on July 31 that three partners simultaneously reported positive results across its royalty and option portfolio: Antimony Resources Corp. returned high-grade antimony-gold drill results at the Bald Mountain property in New Brunswick — strategically important given China's October 2024 export controls on antimony have driven the metal to multi-year highs; Emperor Metals Inc. expanded near-surface gold mineralization at the Duquesne West property in Quebec with 21.3 metres grading 3.0 g/t gold, advancing toward a Preliminary Economic Assessment; and Renforth Resources Inc. reported significant gold-silver surface rock channel results at the Parbec gold project, where Globex holds a 3% Gross Metal Royalty. The Antimony Resources result is particularly timely: antimony is used in flame retardants, ammunition primers, and semiconductor manufacturing, and China's export ban has created the same supply scramble for antimony that earlier controls created for gallium and germanium — making Bald Mountain's high-grade New Brunswick results among the most strategically relevant new drill results in Canada this month.

headline: AMERICA'S RARE EARTH COMEBACK "GATHERING SERIOUS MOMENTUM" — July Closes With All 18 Elements Up; REalloys-Army Military Base Plan Moves Toward 2028 Production Start
snippet: A July 31 analysis argues that the US domestic rare earth supply chain rebuild has crossed from policy announcement into operational momentum, citing REalloys' arrangement to establish the first commercial heavy rare earth processing operation on a US military base (Tooele Army Depot, Utah) for dysprosium and terbium production, Energy Fuels' $104 million rare earth plant at White Mesa Mill (now under construction), and MP Materials' continued expansion — all advancing against the backdrop of a January 1, 2027 Pentagon procurement deadline restricting Chinese-origin rare earth materials in weapons systems. The July 2026 price environment validates the urgency: all 18 tracked rare earth elements rose in price during the month, with the basket averaging a 16.7% monthly gain. For investors in junior rare earth developers, the key tension identified is that while strategic demand is real and prices confirm it, the timeline for domestic US supply to meaningfully substitute Chinese processing remains 2028 or later — which means the 2026-2027 window is characterized by sustained price pressure and limited substitute supply, the ideal price-discovery environment for any North American project moving toward first production.

headline: GDX vs. GDXJ: WHICH WINS THE GOLD BOOM? — As Q2 Earnings Season Closes, Analysts Debate Whether Seniors or Juniors Lead the Next Re-Rating Leg
snippet: With GDX (VanEck Senior Gold Miners ETF) closing the week at $75.74 and GDXJ (Junior Gold Miners) at $97.83 — both up approximately 3% on the week as record Q2 free cash flows from Agnico Eagle ($1.335B), Kinross ($727M), AngloGold ($727M), and Endeavour Mining ($761M H1) landed — the debate among gold equity analysts has shifted from 'if' a re-rating happens to 'who leads it.' The historical pattern in sustained gold bull markets is that senior producers re-rate first on earnings confirmation, then institutional capital rotates into mid-tiers and juniors as the market gains confidence in sustained elevated prices — a sequence that historically accelerates approximately two to four quarters after the first record-earnings quarter for seniors. For retail investors who own TSX-V and ASX exploration and development companies with no Q2 earnings to report, the question of when institutional capital exits the senior ETF and begins shopping junior names is the most actionable allocation question in the sector for H2 2026.

headline: "PERFECT STORM" GOLD SETUP INTACT INTO H2 2026 — Analysts Cite Fed Divided 9-3, Iran Month 6, China Physical Floor, and Record Q2 Margins as Bull Case Foundations
snippet: A Yahoo Finance Canada analysis examines whether the macro conditions driving the gold bull market since 2024 remain intact or are showing signs of structural exhaustion after gold's 28% drawdown from January's $5,596 all-time high to sub-$4,000 in late June. The assessment: the 'perfect storm' thesis holds — a Fed divided 9-3 on July 30 (three hawks voting for immediate hikes) removes the possibility of rate-cutting tailwinds, meaning gold's $4,086 recovery is built on geopolitical and physical demand rather than monetary easing optimism, the more durable foundation. Additional pillars are intact: the US-Iran conflict is now in its sixth month; China's gold imports hit a 2-year monthly high (173 tonnes) in June as retail buyers bought the sub-$4,000 dip at scale; and gold miners delivered record Q2 2026 free cash flows. For junior mining investors holding exploration positions through the June correction, the analysis suggests the autumn seasonality window (typically gold's strongest quarter) is approaching with macro tailwinds still structurally in place.
